title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 5
preview: Two managers tied the median to the hundredth, Brad lost by half a point with the answer on his bench, the commish is on his third kicker since Monday night, and Brian is somehow in first. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Wow, that just happened. What's next? Week 4 gave us a 214.75 beatdown, two teams that scored exactly the median, a commissioner who left the win sitting on his bench, and Coastal Elites going 2-0. Brian Mulvihill is in first place and nobody saw him get there. Week 5 kicks off Thursday, and nobody is safe, least of all the Dictator.
facts_note: Every fact is real Sleeper data: Week 4 results and lineups, transactions through Wednesday Oct 7 (including the 3 AM waiver run and the morning's free-agent moves), injuries, and Week 5 matchups. "Projected" = Sleeper Week 5 projections in league scoring for lineups as set Wednesday around 5:30 PM ET (lineups can change). The look-back compares Week 4 scores to Sleeper's Week 4 projections for the lineups that played. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: The Dictator opened the week trying to bribe the league cop with a little "tip the scale" joke, then got outscored by Drew. A dictator who can't even run a corruption scandal correctly. Emanuel Wilson put up 28.0 on his bench, and Ryan's best possible lineup was 183.5 against Drew's 174.25. The win was sitting right there on the pine and the commissioner looked straight past it. Then he went into Monday night needing a comeback and fell 29.35 short, like a guy sprinting after the bus, slapping the back of it, and watching it pull away. Look-back: projected 151.3, scored 144.9, and my call of a 20-point win was flat wrong. Wednesday he claimed Ryan Fitzgerald at 3:12 AM and cut him for Ka'imi Fairbairn at 8:42 AM. Five and a half hours. That's not a roster move, that's a Tinder match. It's his third kicker since Monday Night Football, and Fairbairn is the kicker Taylor cut in Week 3. Ryan plays Taylor this week. You're dumpster-diving in your opponent's trash, Commish. And he's STILL #1 in the power rankings with a league-high 645.4 points, all from behind a middle-school stache that looks like it's waiting on its learner's permit.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado (2-6). Projected 145.0 to 135.7. Tyler Shough (15.5) sits for Jordan Love (16.8) at superflex, and Braelon Allen (15.1) is on the bench behind Jeremiyah Love (12.6). Emanuel Wilson flashbacks loading.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 10, Fairbairn shanks an extra point, and the Commish is on kicker number four before Thursday night.

entries.roast: The league sweetheart scored exactly 147.9, the median to the hundredth, and tied it. Showed up looking great, did nothing, left early. Parker Washington started and scored 2.0. Devaughn Vele sat on the bench with 17.4. Swap those two and Brad beats Cardillo 163.3 to 162.8. HALF. A. POINT. He lost to Nick Cardillo by a rounding error he personally chose. His Saints defense scored NEGATIVE 5.9, which means the D/ST was technically playing for Cardillo. Look-back: Brad beat his projection by 3.4 and still lost, and I picked him to win, so we both got played. Wednesday he finally cut the Saints D for Cincinnati, dumped Boswell (3.0) for Jake Bates, and claimed Jacoby Brissett to cover Mahomes' bye. A genuinely productive morning. And then he set his lineup and started Parker Washington again.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox. Projected 141.3 to 144.4. Mahomes is on bye, so Brissett (18.3) starts at superflex, and yes, Parker Washington (14.2) starts over Vele (9.8) one more time.
entries.prediction: Brad loses by less than Parker Washington scores, goes quiet, and the chat sends a search party.

entries.roast: Maddox called his shot: he'd lose by the most points this week. And the prophecy came TRUE. Kasik beat him by 66.85, the biggest blowout of the week. Problem is, he also scored exactly 147.9, the median, so he tied the median and ruined his own prophecy halfway through. Even when the man predicts his own failure he can't commit to it. That's spending forty hours on a Minecraft castle and leaving a lava pit through the throne room. Still zero waiver moves all season. His one trade: DK Metcalf for Malik Willis. This week Willis is on the bench projected 15.6 while Stroud starts at 15.9. That's the entire return on a Pro Bowl receiver: a 0.3-point coin flip he doesn't even get to use. Look-back: projected 151.8, scored 147.9, and my lean on Kasik hit, because Gibbs did not go nuclear. He went 17.7.
entries.this_week: vs Brad Kochheiser. Projected 144.4 to 141.3. Bucky Irving is questionable at flex, and Gibbs (25.8) has to carry the whole thing again.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 3, announces it in advance, and the prophecy only half comes true again.

entries.roast: Brian scored 138.8, the second-lowest score of the week, and is now in FIRST PLACE at 6-2. Nobody saw it. Nobody heard it. He just took it. He left 89.3 points on his bench, including Quinshon Judkins' 21.6, and won anyway because his opponent was Taylor. After Brian Robinson scored three touchdowns on Monday night, Brian claimed Brian Robinson at 3:12 AM. A man named Brian adding a guy named Brian, the most human interaction he's had in weeks. Look-back: missed his projection by 9.0, and I had him going 7-1. He went 6-2. Close enough for a ghost. Now Caleb Williams is doubtful and Bryce Young is on bye, so as of tonight Brian's superflex is Malik Washington. A wide receiver. In the quarterback spot. In a superflex league. And we'll hunt him for it. Because he can take it. Because he's not our hero. He's a silent guardian, a watchful protector of first place... a Dark Knight.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano. Projected 128.2 to 144.2. Deshaun Watson starts at QB, Malik Washington (11.3) is in the superflex, Kenneth Walker is on bye, and Brian Robinson (5.3) sits.
entries.prediction: Brian loses by 16, says nothing, and disappears back into the New Mexico night.

entries.roast: 214.75. The week's top score, 59.2 over his projection, the biggest smash in the league, and a 66.85-point beating of the one man who predicted he'd get beat. Nico Collins 33.3. Javonte Williams 31.3 out of the flex. Bijan 30.2. Burrow 29.0. "OH MY GOD! Look at dis! LOOK AT DIS!" Javonte Williams put the team on his back. Look-back: my prediction was that Kasik would win "a close one." It was a 66-point crime scene, counselor. I'd like to file an appeal. I also said Montgomery would score 20 on his bench. He scored 4.3, so for once benching him was actually the right call. Wednesday he finally dropped Quentin Johnston, the guy he started for 2.4 back in Week 3, for the Jaguars defense. Cutting your losses: technically legal advice.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet. Projected 154.7 to 134.9, the highest set lineup in the league. Zay Flowers and Nico Collins are both questionable.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 20, which in his line of work is called a favorable settlement.

entries.roast: A Patriots fan to his core benched two Patriots, Romeo Doubs (23.8) and Rhamondre Stevenson (18.4), and left a league-high 45.8 points on the bench. Gronk would never. He still beat Mike by 7.85, because Mike benched his own tight end even harder. My one clean hit of the week: I said Kyle would win by less than he left on his bench. Book it. Projected 152.2, scored 147.95. Meanwhile, Michigan went to Minnesota for the 100th Little Brown Jug game and lost it, which Kyle will tell you he doesn't care about, from inside the head where Michigan lives rent-free. This week he swapped the Chiefs defense for the Patriots defense and is starting Doubs, Stevenson AND the Pats D, while benching George Kittle for Juwan Johnson. That's not lineup management, that's chasing last week's box score down Route 1.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill. Projected 144.2 to 128.2. Kittle (12.9) and D'Andre Swift (14.7) sit for Juwan Johnson (10.4) and Stevenson (13.3).
entries.prediction: Kyle wins and leaves a Kittle touchdown on the bench, just to keep the tradition alive.

entries.roast: The biggest Vikings fan alive benched the Vikings' tight end. T.J. Hockenson scored 26.9 on Mike's bench. Travis Kelce, starting in his place, scored 3.5. Start Hockenson and Mike beats Kyle 163.5 to 147.95. Instead he lost by 7.85. Careful what you say in the chat, boys, Mike's a cop now. So far the only thing he's locked up is his own tight end. Starting Kelce over Hockenson in 2026 is rolling up to a call in a Crown Vic with a tape deck. The old-head squad (Henry, McCaffrey, Kelce, Evans) isn't a roster, it's a reunion tour with a merch table. Look-back: missed his projection by 7.5, and my "two points either way" was off by almost six. Wednesday he claimed Tyler Huntley, and now Lamar is questionable. Backup plan: Baltimore's backup.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Kasik. Projected 134.9 to 154.7. Kelce is on bye, so Hockenson (10.0) finally starts by default. Lamar is questionable and benched, Kyler Murray and Jalen Hurts are the QBs, and Huntley waits on the bench.
entries.prediction: Mike loses by 20, Hockenson scores 4, and Mike decides the lesson was to start Kelce.

entries.roast: I predicted Drew would go 0-8. Drew went 2-0. He beat the Commish 174.25 to 144.9, beat the median, beat his projection by 48.3, and posted the second-best score of the week behind Kirk Cousins (28.25) and Chuba Hubbard (28.9), which sounds like a personal-injury firm off I-96. The team is called What Parents?, and honestly, whoever raised this man deserves a parade, because he came out swinging like somebody taught him right. Drew has always said Tuesday Night Hockey beats Monday Night Football, and for one week he was right: Ryan needed MNF, and MNF said no. This week he's benching Jayden Daniels (questionable, 16.8 projected) for Kirk Cousins (15.0) and Geno Smith (14.1), and starting two tight ends like it's a Lions goal-line package.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo. Projected 125.1 to 119.7, a showdown between last week's two surprise 2-0 teams. Puka Nacua is questionable, and Daniels sits.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 6 and goes 2-0 again. I'm not doubting the man twice in a row.

entries.roast: Week 1, Taylor scored 232.5, the highest score of the season. Week 4, 111.7, the lowest score of the week. Champagne to tap water in three weeks. His week went sideways early and never came back, and he missed his projection by 21.6, the worst miss in the league. A man who hands out nicknames like a rally speech has earned one: Low-Energy Taylor. Sad, but true! In Week 2 he dropped Aaron Rodgers for Marcus Mariota. At 3:12 this morning he dropped Mariota to claim Aaron Rodgers back. That's not a waiver claim, that's texting your ex at 3 AM. And last week I predicted Taylor would grab a seventh defense out of pure spite. At 8:14 this morning he picked up Washington. Count 'em: Patriots, Jaguars, Bucs, Giants, Browns, Bears, Commanders. SEVEN. I don't make predictions, I make prophecies. Unlike Maddox.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer. Projected 135.7 to 145.0. Justin Jefferson (16.5) is back in the lineup but questionable, Aaron Rodgers is at superflex, and Ryan is kicking with Ka'imi Fairbairn, the kicker Taylor cut in Week 3.
entries.prediction: Taylor loses by 9, Fairbairn hits the dagger, and defense number eight arrives by Sunday.

entries.roast: Coastal Elites went 2-0 off the lowest projection in the league, beat it by 44.5, and my 1-7 prediction is now a framed piece of evidence against me. Tetairoa McMillan scored 46.2. Not long ago Cardillo was practically begging the league to take his receivers. Then Mike offered Josh Jacobs and a first for McMillan, and Cardillo gave the whole chat a lecture on fair trade value. Now McMillan drops 46.2 and the asking price is a first, a kidney, and Mike's squad car. Meanwhile UMass started 4-0, sold out for the first time since 2014, and then lost 38-14 to Eastern Michigan, the exact same week Cardillo's team finally showed up. Massachusetts only gets one competent football team at a time, and this week it was the fantasy one. He also left Carnell Tate's 21.5 on the bench and still won, which is the first time all year the universe has cut him a break. Wednesday's move: dropped Dontayvion Wicks and added nobody.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman. Projected 119.7 to 125.1, the lowest set lineup in the league again. McMillan is on bye, so the king's-ransom receiver is off the showroom floor for a week. Two QBs (Lawrence 18.2, Maye 19.4) and Carnell Tate (12.1) carry the load.
entries.prediction: Cardillo loses by 6 and raises McMillan's price anyway.
